title: Medicare Scam Calls Threaten to Cancel Benefits
how_it_works: Scammers call pretending to be from Medicare, saying your benefits will be canceled unless you give them personal information or pay a fee. They try to scare you into acting quickly.
example_message: "This is Medicare. Your benefits will be canceled unless you confirm your Social Security number and pay a small fee today."
red_flags: Caller says your benefits will be canceled
Asks for your Social Security number or bank info
Pressures you to act right away
what_to_do: Hang up and call Medicare directly at 1-800-MEDICARE if you have questions.

title: Fake Tech Support Pop-Ups on Your Computer
how_it_works: You see a pop-up on your computer warning about a virus and telling you to call a phone number for help. If you call, scammers pretend to be from Microsoft or Apple and ask for money or access to your computer.
example_message: "Warning! Your computer is infected. Call Microsoft support now at 1-888-123-4567."
red_flags: Pop-up says you have a virus and gives a phone number
Person asks for remote access to your computer
They want you to pay with gift cards or wire transfer
what_to_do: Close the pop-up and do not call the number. If you’re worried, ask a trusted friend or family member for help.

title: Social Security Text Message Scam
how_it_works: You get a text saying there’s a problem with your Social Security account. The message includes a link and says you must click it to fix the issue. The link leads to a fake website that steals your information.
example_message: "Alert: There is a problem with your Social Security account. Click here to resolve: [fake link]"
red_flags: Text says there’s a problem with your Social Security
what_to_do: Delete the message and do not click any links.

title: Grandparent Emergency Scam
how_it_works: You get a call from someone pretending to be your grandchild or a lawyer. They say your grandchild is in trouble and needs money right away, often for bail or an emergency.
example_message: "Grandma, it’s me. I’m in jail and need you to send money right away. Please don’t tell mom and dad."
red_flags: Caller says it’s urgent and asks for secrecy
Wants money sent by wire or gift cards
You’re told not to tell anyone
what_to_do: Hang up and call your grandchild or another family member to check if the story is true.

title: Romance Scams on Facebook and Dating Sites
how_it_works: Someone you meet online quickly says they love you and need money for an emergency or travel. They make excuses for why they can’t meet in person and keep asking for more money.
example_message: "I care about you so much, but I need help paying for a plane ticket to come see you. Can you send me $500?"
red_flags: Person you’ve never met asks for money
They have lots of excuses and urgent needs
what_to_do: Stop communicating and never send money to someone you haven’t met in person.
